newsitem.title: USA: Olin Corp has no plans to appeal Superfund case.
newsitem.headline: Olin Corp has no plans to appeal Superfund case.

text.p: Olin Corp said Thursday it was unlikely to appeal a court decision holding the company responsible for cleaning up toxic waste at its chemical plant site in McIntosh, Alabama.
"We have not had a chance to thoroughly review the decision. But at this point we have no plans to take further court action," Olin Corp spokesman Bill McDaniel said.

The U.S. Court of Appeals 11th Circuit Tuesday reversed a lower court decision that would have let Olin off the hook for paying to clean up the contamination on its property under the Superfund toxic waste law.

Three appeals court judges in Atlanta unanimously rejected Olin's argument that the Superfund law could not be used to make companies clean sites where they had dumped waste legally before the Superfund law was passed, and where environmental damage was only on the company's property.

Olin has already begun design work to get rid of the waste at the Alabama site under an agreement with the Environmental Protection Agency. "We have said all along that we were committed to cleaning it up regardless of the outcome of the court case," McDaniel said.

The Justice Department Thursday hailed the court's ruling, which upheld the Clinton administration's position that polluters must pay to clean messes they created, even if they dumped the waste legally.
